REASONING:

Step 1 - Frame the project
- Objective: Improve the effectiveness and coordination of selected public programs to alleviate constraints to competitiveness and job creation (investment/export promotion, innovation, active labor market programs, labor intermediation, activation of social assistance beneficiaries).
- Scope: Part A - Results-Based Financing (EUR 85.025m) reimbursing Eligible Expenditure Programs (EEPs) upon achieving Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) across four components; Part B - Project Management & Technical Assistance (EUR 4.25m). Total Project Financing: EUR 89.5m IBRD loan (USD 100m equivalent) out of total project cost EUR 352.48m.
- Components: 
  1. Policy planning, monitoring, and coordination (EUR 3.6m)
  2. Investment and export promotion (EUR 19.7m)
  3. Innovation (EUR 31.3m: enterprise innovation, technology transfer facility, public RDI reforms)
  4. Labor (EUR 30.4m: NES intermediation, ALMPs, social assistance activation)
  Part B: Project Management and TA (EUR 4.25m)
- Delivery Model: Investment Project Financing (IPF) with DLIs for Part A and traditional Statement of Expenditure (SOE) disbursements for Part B.
- Timeline: Project implementation start 26-Aug-2015; closing date 30-Jun-2019.
- Budget: EUR 89.5 million IBRD loan; Borrower co-financing EUR 262.98 million (Total EEPs EUR 348m).
- Key Stakeholders: Public Policy Secretariat (PPS - main coordinator), Ministry of Economy (MoE), Ministry of Education, Science and Technological Development (MoESTD) / Innovation Fund, Ministry of Labor, Employment, Veteran and Social Affairs (MoLEVSA) / National Employment Service (NES), Ministry of Finance.
- External Dependencies: IMF Precautionary Stand-By Agreement; parallel donor initiatives (EU IPA trust funds, USAID, EIB, EBRD).

Step 2 - Category sweep
- technical:
  - High caseworker caseloads in NES branch offices (up to 2,000+ per worker) dilute client focus and job matching quality (PAD p. 11, 46).
  - High tax wedges and 1-to-1 benefit withdrawal disincentivize social assistance recipients from accepting formal work (PAD p. 11, 52).
  - Public R&D institutes (RDIs) are disconnected from industry needs and generate little commercial value (PAD p. 10, Annex 2 p. 35).
- financial:
  - Fiscal austerity, wage cuts, and budget constraints threaten sustained funding for ALMPs and matching grants (PAD p. 11, 50, Annex 3 p. 25).
  - Interruption of grant financing due to reliance on donor funds (e.g., IF unable to launch matching grant calls in 2015) (PAD p. 9, 39).
- schedule:
  - Risks of delay in meeting effectiveness conditions, such as establishing the PIU in PPS and hiring key fiduciary experts (PAD p. vi, 80).
- stakeholder:
  - Perceived high level of national corruption potentially hindering transparent procurement and execution (PAD Annex 4 p. 32).
- political_regulatory:
  - Political economy constraints and intermittent leadership hindering deep structural reforms in public research institutes (PAD p. 10, 43, Annex 3 p. 17).
- environmental:
  - Potential localized environmental risks arising from innovative technology/industrial sub-projects under Mini and Matching Grants (PAD p. 23, 90).
- organizational:
  - Weak policy planning, coordination, and M&E capacity across line ministries (PAD p. 3, 11).
  - Lack of World Bank procurement and fiduciary familiarity within PPS, MoE, and MoLEVSA (PAD p. 23, 86, Annex 4 p. 28).
  - Fragmented, overlapping mandates and non-transparent performance history among MoE agencies (SIEPA, Development Fund, AOFI, NARR) (PAD p. 7, 29, Annex 3 p. 12).
- external:
  - Severe macroeconomic shocks or natural disasters (e.g., 2014 floods) destabilizing reform implementation (PAD p. 1, 1).

Step 3 - Evidence filter
All candidate risks noted above are anchored directly in specific textual statements from the Appraisal Document.

Step 4 - Assess
Each risk is evaluated for Likelihood (1-5) and Impact (1-5) based on severity, institutional context, and historical baseline described in the text, accompanied by concrete mitigations grounded in the PAD's proposed TA and DLI mechanisms.

Step 5 - Consolidate
Merged related institutional capacity items and refined the list into 13 distinct, well-evidenced risks across all valid categories.
